prompt: What defines Lívia's position as an internal consultant?

choices.text: She is paid by each team for her hours
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson describes internal billing.

choices.text: She only advises, and never builds anything herself
choices.why: She builds plenty elsewhere; the position is about ownership, not activity.

choices.text: She helps with problems that are not hers
choices.why: Right: by people free to ignore her, so everything she achieves comes from being useful enough to be listened to.

choices.text: She has authority over every team's architecture
choices.why: The lesson says the opposite: she cannot order anybody.

prompt: Put Peter Block's phases in order.
items: Feedback and the decision to act

prompt: Where does Block say most consulting failures are decided?

choices.text: In discovery, when the wrong data is collected
choices.why: Bad data is a failure, but Block places most of them earlier.

choices.text: In contracting, the first phase, before any data is collected
choices.why: Right: they become visible at feedback, as an answer to a question nobody thought they asked.

choices.text: At the end, when nobody agrees whether to continue
choices.why: An ending without a decision is a symptom, not the origin.

choices.text: In engagement, when the work turns out harder than expected
choices.why: Late, and not where Block puts it.

prompt: Weinberg's second law of consulting: no matter how it looks at first, it's always a ___ problem.
What question did the contract replace "help us pick a message broker" with?
hint: A broker becomes one possible answer.

choices.text: Should Marola standardise on one broker across all its teams?
choices.why: Wider, and still about the solution.

choices.text: Who broke route planning?
choices.why: Blame is explicitly out of scope.

choices.text: Which message broker fits logistics best?
choices.why: That is the original request, narrowed.

choices.text: Why do releases break route planning, and what would stop it?
choices.why: Right: the problem, with the broker as one candidate.

prompt: Match each line of the contract to the failure it prevents.

pairs.right: a recommendation treated as an order, or ignored
help that becomes an open-ended favour
being drawn into blame or into building it
a final report that surprises the client

right_distractors: a broker chosen without comparing alternatives

prompt: Why does Lívia say out loud, at the start of every interview, that she is not evaluating the team?
hint: What do members of a team that asked for help wonder?

choices.text: Henrique required it in writing
choices.why: He did not ask for it.

choices.text: So the interviews are honest
choices.why: Right: people wonder whether the helper is also reporting on them.

choices.text: To make the interviews shorter by skipping performance topics
choices.why: Length is not the reason.

choices.text: Company policy forbids evaluations by staff engineers
choices.why: No such policy appears in the lesson.

prompt: 7 of 23 releases were followed by an incident. What percentage is that, to the nearest whole number?
Why does Lívia use the data, the people and the system rather than one of them?

choices.text: The contract required exactly three sources
choices.why: It asked for data access and interviews; three is not a rule.

choices.text: To make the final report look thorough
choices.why: Appearance is not the reason.

choices.text: Because the interviews contradicted the data and needed a tie-break
choices.why: They agreed; the people explained what the data showed.

choices.text: Each has a blind spot; together they mostly cancel
choices.why: Right: the data cannot say why, people believe folklore, and the system confirms or not.

prompt: Paulo says a broker would let "each service have its own copy of the data, and nobody could break anybody else". What did Lívia read in that sentence?
hint: What would the broker spare them?

choices.text: That the broker was the correct answer after all
choices.why: None of the incidents was a timeout; the broker was wanted for another reason.

choices.text: That Paulo understood brokers better than anybody
choices.why: His expertise is not what the sentence revealed.

choices.text: A way out of negotiating who owns the table
choices.why: Right: the people problem, stating itself in technical words.

choices.text: That the zone service team should be replaced
choices.why: Nobody said that, and blame was out of scope.

prompt: Which hypotheses did the evidence support? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The shared table has no owner and no contract
choices.why: Yes: five of seven incidents.

choices.text: The two services are only tested together after merging
choices.why: Yes: all seven found in staging or production.

choices.text: The services need asynchronous messaging
choices.why: No timeouts in any incident.

prompt: How many of the seven incidents came from a change to the shared table?
hint: The longest row of the figure.

prompt: Why does the written note give facts, then interpretation, then recommendation, each labelled?
hint: A reader who disagrees with one part.

choices.text: The findings survive a rejected recommendation
choices.why: Right: which keeps the conversation going.

choices.text: It is the company template for every document
choices.why: The lesson argues for it, not from a template.

choices.text: So the recommendation is the last thing remembered
choices.why: A rhetorical trick the lesson does not mention.

choices.text: Because the decider reads only the last paragraph of a note
choices.why: Lesson 1 says readers read the top, not the bottom.

prompt: Why does the note keep the broker, as option 3?

choices.text: For the right reason, it would help
choices.why: Right: Henrique's instinct was aimed at a symptom, not wrong, and saying where it fits helps the diagnosis land.

choices.text: Because the zone service team had already agreed to it
choices.why: The note says it needs that team's time, not that they agreed.

choices.text: To be polite, since Henrique asked for a broker
choices.why: Politeness alone would be a fake option; this one is real.

choices.text: Because it is the cheapest option
choices.why: It is the most expensive, about a quarter.

prompt: The note does not say whose change broke what. Why?

choices.text: Names are confidential under company policy
choices.why: Not the reason given.

choices.text: Henrique asked her to leave names out
choices.why: He did not need to; the contract already did.

choices.text: Evaluating people was out of scope
choices.why: Right: how people work together, not who failed.

choices.text: To protect Paulo, who made most of the changes
choices.why: The lesson never says who made them, and protecting anyone is not the reason.

prompt: Henrique hears the diagnosis and chooses option 1 instead of the recommended option 2. What should Lívia do, by the lesson?

choices.text: Escalate to Otávio, since the evidence clearly favours option 2 over option 1
choices.why: Winning over the owner's head loses the engagement and the next call.

choices.text: Argue until he agrees, since the data is clear
choices.why: A consultant who wins the argument has usually lost the engagement.

choices.text: Withdraw her help, since the advice was ignored
choices.why: The owner chose; the consultant helps with what was chosen.

choices.text: Write down her advice and why, then help with what he chose
choices.why: Right: the note is the record; the relationship gets the next call.

prompt: Sofia, the support lead, asks Lívia to "add a chatbot to cut support tickets". Which first step follows this lesson?

choices.text: Tell Sofia chatbots rarely work
choices.why: A verdict before any listening or data.

choices.text: Compare three chatbot vendors and send the table
choices.why: That accepts the request as the question.

choices.text: Read the ticket data tonight and present a full diagnosis the next morning
choices.why: Discovery before contracting, and a diagnosis nobody agreed to ask for.

choices.text: Agree the question, who decides, what she delivers and what is out
choices.why: Right: contracting comes first, and the question may change.
